content: The external orifice of the uterus, also known as the ostium of the uterus or external os, is a small, depressed, and somewhat circular opening located at the rounded extremity of the vaginal portion of the cervix. This opening serves as the communication point between the cervical cavity and the vaginal cavity. The external orifice is bordered by two lips: an anterior lip and a posterior lip. The anterior lip is shorter and thicker, but it projects lower than the posterior lip due to the natural slope of the cervix. Under normal conditions, both lips are in contact with the posterior vaginal wall. Before pregnancy, the external orifice typically has a rounded shape when observed through the vaginal canal, such as during a speculum examination. However, after childbirth (parturition), the shape of the orifice changes, resembling a transverse slit or taking on an H-shaped appearance.
